Description: This is a Request for Quote (RFQ). The Government anticipates awarding a firm-fixed price contract resulting from this solicitation. All respondents must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at www.sam.gov and certified by the SBA in Small Business Search (SBS). Interested SDVOSB s must be listed to receive contract awards. Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office 16, is soliciting offers for Switchgear (Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS) Investigation and Repair. The service will be provided to (GVSMVAMC) G.V. Sonny Montgomery VA Medical Center in Jackson MS, in accordance with the Statement of Work (SOW). Site Visit: Date/Time Location POC Tuesday November 10th from 9:00am to 1:00pm. G. V. (Sonny) Montgomery VA Medical Center 1500 E Woodrow Wilson Drive Jackson, MS 39216 Willard Bill Rushing Facility Operations Supervisor Cell: 601-559-7104 Willard.Rushing@va.gov TECHNICAL QUESTIONS: All questions shall be received by Thursday November 12, 2026, at 4:00 P.M. CST. All questions submitted for this solicitation shall me electronically sent to the following email address: Vanessaann.Williams@va.gov. Please title email with the Solicitation Number, Technical Questions . Questions shall clearly identify which part of the solicitation. Questions received after the date stated may be addressed at the discretion of the Contracting Officer. Answers to questions will be addressed via an amendment to the solicitation posted to www.sams.gov. OFFER INSTRUCTIONS: 1. All offers are due NLT Wednesday, November 18, 2026, at 4:00 P.M. CST via e-mail only to Vanessaann.Williams@va.gov. Quotes shall be received on or before the date and time specified in Block 8 of the Standard Form (SF) 1449. Please title email with Solicitation Number, Proposal Submission, Vendor Name . 2. Offeror must complete and return the signed SF 1449, blocks 30a, 30b, and 30c. By signing the Standard Form (SF) 1449/Solicitation, the contractor attests acknowledgement and understanding of all solicitation requirements. 3. If applicable, must acknowledge receipt of all solicitation amendments by the offer due time/date specified, if applicable, by (a) Returning a signed copy of each amendment or (b) Acknowledging receipt of amendment on each copy of the quote or (c) By separate electronic communication which includes a reference to the solicitation and amendment numbers. 4. Offeror must submit the Price/Cost Schedule with unit prices rounded to the nearest hundredth. Please ensure unit price and total amounts are correct. Offeror agrees to hold the price in its offer firm for 60 calendar days from the date specified for receipt of offers. 5. Offeror must complete, sign, and return VAAR Clause 852.219-75 VA NOTICE OF LIMITATIONS ON SUBCONTRACTING CERTIFICATE OF COMPLIANCE FOR SERVICES AND CONSTRUCTION (JAN 2023) (DEVIATION). 6. Offeror shall submit a Capability Statement that demonstrates their aptitude for working on these systems to include: Investigation Tasks: Inspect and evaluate: GE Main switchgear (MV, LV sections as applicable) ABB Distribution switchgear sections ASCO ATS-1 and ATS-2 (including logic boards, transfer mechanism, control power circuits) Identify voltage ratings of trip and close coils. Rack breakers out for physical inspection. Perform mechanical integrity inspection (linkages, springs, shutters, rails). Evaluate relay configuration: GE Multilin F-60, G-30, MIF II, UR-series relays, ABB relays. Review protective relay event logs. Verify battery health for control relays. Inspect control wiring and MOC/TOC blocks. Document all deficiencies discovered. Repair Tasks: Replace trip coils/close coils where improper voltages or failures are found. Replace or repair MOC/TOC blocks. Replace relay control batteries. Repair/replace defective relays (G-30, Multilin series, if field-repairable, ABB). Correct wiring faults, loose lugs, damaged insulation. ATS logic troubleshooting and repair (ASCO control board testing, timing sequence validation, mechanical). Functional testing of each breaker after repair. Re-racking, lubrication, cleaning, and cabinet maintenance Generator/ATS Integration Testing (as needed) Support load-bank verification of generator response (coordination with CAT dealer). Remove/reconnect bias signals during generator tuning (if required). Deliverables Investigation Report identifying all deficiencies. Repair Completion Report summarizing corrective actions performed. Updated device condition log for the switchgear, ATS units, and relays. Recommendations for future reliability improvements. It is the responsibility of the quoter to submit sufficient information to convey their technical capability in meeting the requirements of the Statement of Work. Failure to provide sufficient information will result in the quote being considered not technically acceptable. 7. Provide a list of three (3) other concerns and/or Government agencies for which services similar in size and scope were rendered by the Offeror over the past three years. The list must include name of contact, organization, a valid email address, valid phone number, dollar value of project, and description of the project.

Title: Enhanced Use Leasing Project Edwards Air Force Base
Description: The Department of the Air Force (“DAF”) is accepting proposals for the development of market facing mixed-use projects to include, but not limited to, housing accessible to military families and/or single members, civilians and defense contractors, medical facilities, and commercial/retail space (“Projects”). As consideration for leasing its parcels to developers selected under this RFLP, DAF is seeking cash rent and/or in-kind consideration (IKC) including future, undetermined construction projects. Pursuant to the foregoing Executive Order and the Enabling Statute, the Department of the Air Force (the “Government”) is issuing this Request for Lease Proposal (the “RFLP”) to solicit proposals from entities (“Offeror(s)”) interested in entering into a long-term ground lease (the “Lease”) to lease all or a portion of that certain real property located at Edwards AFB (the “Installation”), which is an active military installation located in Kern County, California comprised of two parcels totaling approximately 215-acres of land (the “Property”) from the Government for the purposes of financing, permitting, developing, constructing, installing, owning, maintaining and operating improvements upon the Property for the Lessee’s private commercial (non-Federal government) use (collectively, the “Project”). In accordance with and subject to the terms, requirements, and conditions of this RFLP, the Government will evaluate all proposals received to select one or more Offerors as a “Potential Lessee(s)” with whom to enter lease negotiations. A Potential Lessee with whom the Government makes and enters into a written and legally binding lease agreement is hereinafter referred to as a “Lessee.” If no agreement is made, a Potential Lessee may not actually become a Lessee.

Title: Apache Alert Mission Complex
Description: Pre-Solicitation Notice for Apache Alert Mission Complex Anticipated Solicitation Issue Date: November 2026 Anticipated Solicitation Response Date: December 2026 Set Aside: As the work will be performed outside of the continental United States, no set asides to small business or socioeconomic preference for this solicitation. NAICS: 236220 -- Commercial and Industrial Building Construction, and the Small Business Size Standard is $45,000,000. Contracting Office Address: US Army Corps of Engineers – Middle East District, 201 Prince Frederick Drive, Winchester, VA, 22602 SYNOPSIS: SWM is anticipating a Design-Bid-Build (DBB) award for the Construction of facilities to support and enhance the Apache Alert Mission at Ali Al Salem Air Base in the country of Kuwait. PROJECT SCOPE: The facilities to be constructed include: Four Alert Shelters with Aprons Logistics Readiness Center Maintenance Supply Warehouse with Exterior Storage Shade Guard House Pilot Readiness Facility Petroleum Oil Lubricant (POL) Shed Fire Water Pump House with Water Tank Alert Magazine (option) Forward Arming and Refueling Point (FARP) Parking Sunshades Bunkers Three Electrical Substations All site utilities, incl. Stormwater, Domestic Water, Fire Water, Sanitary Sewer with Lift Station and Leach Field, and Site Electrical and Communications Site Development, incl. Taxiway, Vehicular Pavement, and Parking Lot Helipad and Taxiway Rehabilitation (option) Hardened Aircraft Shelter (HAS) Demolition (option) FARP Expansion (option) Paved Access to Practice Runway (option) The project includes all utilities, site improvements, new concrete aprons, airfield and vehicular pavements, detection and protection features, security enhancements, and other supporting work necessary to construct complete and useable facilities. The project is phased to maintain uninterrupted airfield and squadron alert and training operations during construction. The Period of Performance is anticipated to be 1,355 calendar days from issuance of Notice to Proceed. PROPOSAL PROCEDURES: The Request for Proposal (RFP) will be issued on SAM.GOV. It is anticipated that the Best Value Trade-Off (BVTO) contracting method will be used to evaluate proposals. Evaluation criteria will be stated in the RFP. RESPONSE PERIOD: This is a pre-solicitation notice and is not a request for proposal (RFP) nor does it restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. A response to this notice is not required. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparation of a response to this notice. Questions can be sent to Maria Martin, e-mail: Maria.L.Martin@usace.army.mil and Tracy Gusukuma, e-mail: tracy.m.gusukuma@usace.army.mil.
